claims.text: Gaius’s translated law distinguishes specified Rome actions from those dependent on magistrate imperium. Athens’s translated oil law assigns cases to civic bodies and allows imperial or proconsular appeal. These are different operative jurisdictions, not one uniform imperial procedure. The fragmentary inscription and uncollated editions establish prescriptions, not universal enforcement or complete endpoint office rosters.

claims.text: What defeats the inference from shared empire to identical jurisdiction? The specified Rome conditions and magistrate-term distinction differ from Athens’s civic decision makers and imperial/proconsular appeal.
claims.source: https://droitromain.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/Anglica/gai4_Poste.htm; Book IV §§103–105, web L145–150; selected representation SHA256 9b390d1d56c99383ccc548513e6290530591b17c049977a30d0b3ffa1ce48989; https://www.atticinscriptions.com/inscription/IGII2/1100; translation, web L14–21; selected representation SHA256 aeb29fc5a77e88dc08e0c8f0faca63075d872721556f55ce129614aeb1b57bab; https://droitromain.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/Anglica/gai4_Poste.htm; Book IV §§104–109; selected representation SHA256 9b390d1d56c99383ccc548513e6290530591b17c049977a30d0b3ffa1ce48989; https://www.atticinscriptions.com/inscription/IGII2/1100; web L20–21; selected representation SHA256 aeb29fc5a77e88dc08e0c8f0faca63075d872721556f55ce129614aeb1b57bab
